text:
rachel: Hey team — incoming from BrightAnalytics. After they accepted an org transfer their automation fails when trying to DELETE project `ba-prod`. API returns 403 with `insufficient_scope` and message `caller lacks permission to delete project`.
noah: Can you paste the curl they're using and the token type? (api key vs delegated token)
rachel: Pasted below (redacted):
```
curl -X DELETE https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/ba-prod \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...REDACTED..." \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```
They said token was created by their CI service account after the org transfer completed.
liz: Quick thought — org transfer can cause role bindings to be re-evaluated. If their token is scoped to `read:projects` or is an ephemeral delegated token tied to the old org audience it will 403. Can you ask for the token `scope`/`aud` from the token introspection? (we have introspect endpoint: `POST /v1/tokens/introspect`)
sam: Also check whether the service account's role is still bound to the target org/project after transfer. We sometimes see a timing window where the console shows the role but backend role bindings haven't fully reconciled.
idp-bot: [automated log extract] request_id=rc-8a7f delete_project ba-prod -> 403 PERM_DENIED {reason: "insufficient_scope", required_scopes: ["admin:projects:create","admin:projects:delete"], token_audience: "ci-service@old-org"}
support-engineer: Thanks — that log is super helpful. Looks like token audience is still `ci-service@old-org`. Repro steps I recommend:
1) Revoke the old token and generate a new service token scoped for the new org (`admin:projects:delete`).
2) If they use OIDC/SSO, ensure the token audience claim matches the new org (we've seen `aud` stuck to old org until a SCIM resync).
3) On our side, run a role-binding reconciliation for the customer's org: `POST /internal/admin/reconcile-bindings?org=brightanalytics` (I'll run with ops permissions).
noah: Can you share minimal repro? I can run with a throwaway org to confirm race.
rachel: Repro sequence from customer:
- org transfer accepted at 2025-11-02T14:12Z
- CI job triggered at 14:13Z which used previously-issued token
- API returned 403 at 14:13:05Z
- They rotated token at 14:15Z -> same 403 until we reconciled
support-engineer: I'm kicking off reconcile now. Also requested they create a fresh token with `--scopes admin:projects:delete,admin:projects:update` and try again.
idp-bot: [audit] reconcile job queued by support-engineer (job id rc-recon-1790012345-1)
liz: FYI: I checked the SCIM sync logs — there was a transient failure at 14:10Z during the transfer which left the service principal `ci-service` temporarily mapped to the old org audience. That explains the `aud` in the log.
support-engineer: Reconcile finished: job rc-recon-1790012345-1 -> success. I also applied a targeted role rebind for `ci-service@new-org`.
rachel: Customer tried delete after that, success: 204 No Content. They say regenerating the token alone didn't fix it until we reconciled bind.
sam: Good catch. Root cause summary for the ticket: token audience and role bindings stale after org transfer due to transient SCIM sync failure. Fix: reconcile bindings + regen token with correct scopes. Follow-up: we'll add a check in the org-transfer flow to block transfer completion until SCIM re-check passes.
noah: Suggest adding a small KB article and a one-liner CLI diagnostic: `redwood auth:check --token <token>` which returns audience/scopes and recommended action.
rachel: I'll update the support ticket and send the KB draft to docs. Customer confirmed no further issues and asked to be notified if we roll out the CLI check.
support-engineer: Closing thread once docs PR is in. :white_check_mark:
